analysis.title: UBS TECH DAILY CURT COMMENT: 3 big calls today
key_insights: Last week: SXXP -1.4%, SPX -0.5%, SX8P -0.1%, SOXX -3%, IGV +6%. Software outperformed semis again.

Atlassian and Adobe were up 10% and 7.5% w/w. SAP was up 7% w/w on a solid print. Most other software names were up low-to-mid single digits. Semis were weak: mid caps down high single digits, bigger semis down low-to-mid single digits.

Curtis's bearish view is that hyperscalers cannot keep running negative FCF unless top-of-funnel revenue per GW contracted rises. He says the view is now resonating, and client calls have moved to assessing top-down ecosystems and what could win once sentiment troughs.

He wants more balanced corporate commentary and says Jensen being bullish is no longer helpful. He describes three phases: phase 1 up, phase 2 reset, phase 3 a more considered build-out where those with unencumbered capacity could do very well. Phase 2 share prices probably have more downside.
Second and third derivatives support the bearish WFE view. LRCX fell 12% on Thursday after already being down 40% from the peak.

Leverage with rising cost of debt/CDS is a bad combination. He estimates that once the first 15-20GW of capacity is built each year, anything on top is funded by borrowed money. He bases this on the big 4 hyperscalers each building about 1GW per quarter and now being FCF negative.

Meta: headline numbers were solid, but the print did not resolve the bigger questions. The new share class does not come into play until Jan 2027, which pushes new financing into 1H27 along with real 2027 OpEx/CapEx guidance. Muse monetization is not expected until 2027+, so EPS compression and negative FCF concerns (which META officially hit) get louder.

Meta's 8K discusses raising hundreds of billions of dollars over several years. Class C non-voting shares give Meta a currency to raise capital without diluting Zuckerberg's voting control. The CFO flagged significant investments and rising total serving costs.
Weekly moves through Thursday: Meta -8%, Google -5%, Oracle -2%, CRWV -10%, MSFT -1.5%, AMZN flat.

SAP: Q3 current cloud backlog (CCB) grew 26% ccy vs 25% bogey, after 26% ccy in Q2. Q3 P&L was ahead by 2.4% at EBIT level. Guide reiterated with cloud and software revenue at the upper end of the range. Curtis does not expect numbers to move much.
TXN: MSD% EBIT beat and a Q4 revenue guide of flat q/q vs seasonal down MSD%. The stock fell 1.8% Thursday post print and was up 1% w/w. Curtis says TXN set the scene for semis/analog.

Nokia: Q3 sales +9% ccy, a small beat, with EBIT 30% ahead due to opex in the mobile division. The FY guide reiteration did not carry the beat. Nokia sees optical and IP networks growing 25-30% in 2027 vs Street c20%. The stock fell 10% Thursday and 12.5% w/w.

Besi: positive hybrid bonding narrative and a very good Q3 order book, but a small Q3 EBIT beat and a Q4 miss. Besi is running a strategic review of customer roadmaps over five years and will likely present findings at Q4 results, which Curtis sees as a key catalyst.
LRCX: good FQ1, but revenue guide slightly below UBS model and bogeys on minor supply chain disruptions, with evidence of pricing power and share gains. The stock was down 13% w/w to Thursday.
Computacenter pre-release: 2026 PBT guide raised from >£380m to >£425m vs bogey c£410m. Backlog updated from £9.3bn to £12.6bn.

ORCL Investor Day (10/28): sentiment is deeply negative on levered AI infrastructure names and bullish inbounds have dropped off. Focus will be financing and debt. Karl thinks a financing plan with a range of external financing needs landing at the low end would calm people. Capex growth next year determines the funding gap.

MSFT (10/28): consensus long, with sentiment 9/10. Karl Keirstead believes the fundamentals support higher buyside expectations. His F1Q Azure bogey is a 2pt beat at 47% growth. Drivers are OpenAI upside, GPU inflation and capacity adds, plus M365 upside from usage-based pricing.

GOOGL (10/28): still the consensus funding short across megacaps, sentiment 4/10, HFs short and LOs overweight but biased to downside. Concerns are search cannibalization and the Gemini delay. Investors want a credible AI agent and a broader Gemini 4 rollout.

AMZN (10/29): very crowded long, sentiment 9/10. Debates are AWS margins and agentic risk. Investors look for low-40s AWS growth and margins, and anything short of that could weigh on sentiment into year end. 3P data points to some softness in NA retail.
